BRED Bank Fiji Advances Payments Modernisation with BPC SmartVista
summary:
BRED Bank Fiji, part of the BRED Group, has reached a key milestone in its international payments modernisation journey with BPC, a global leader in payment solutions. All active Visa and private-label cards in Fiji have now been migrated to BPC’s cloud-based SmartVista issuing platform, following the earlier modernisation of acquiring services. 
The migration is part of BRED Group’ wider deployment of SmartVista across its international markets. The platform gives BRED Bank Fiji a scalable infrastructure to launch new card programmes faster and improve the consistency and security of its payment services. 
Customers and merchants can now benefit from broader acceptance of international cards, supporting domestic, cross-border and e-commerce payments. Across its live markets, BRED Group is better equipped to support merchants with contactless and multi-currency acceptance, purchase with cash-out, pre-authorisation, cash advance, tips, refunds, reversals, multi-currency settlement and digital merchant onboarding. As the latest acquiring milestone, BRED Bank Fiji will integrate its payment gateway into the modern platform, strengthening online payment processing and enabling a faster, more secure checkout experience. 
BRED Bank Fiji has also selected BPC’s AI-powered SmartVista Fraud Management solution to protect transactions across ATM, point-of-sale and e-commerce channels. 
“The successful migration in Fiji gives us a modern and scalable platform to strengthen card issuing, improve customer services and support our future growth,” said Pierre-Antoine Vallet, Deputy CEO and Chief Financial and Information Officer at BRED Bank Fiji. “With BPC as our technology partner, we can continue to develop more convenient, secure and accessible payment services.” 
Georgy Rashin, Head of Delivery APAC at BPC, added: “We are proud to support BRED Bank Fiji in this major milestone and to provide BRED Group with a consistent platform across its international markets. SmartVista will help the Group strengthen payment acceptance and deliver secure digital services at scale.” 
The next stages of the programme will include further issuing enhancements, virtual cards, cardless withdrawals, UPI card acceptance and new merchant portals.

Ripjar ramps up AI in customer screening to disrupt global economy of crime
summary:
Ripjar, the provider of smarter screening and risk intelligence solutions, has introduced new AI innovations within ULTRA, the real intelligence engine that powers screening operations at financial institutions and enterprises, including 25% of the Global Systemically Important Banks and 35+ of the Global Fortune 500. The updates enable compliance teams to identify and manage risk with greater confidence, speed and clarity, making screening more intelligent, explainable and actionable at scale. 
Built on national security grade technology, ULTRA delivers a level of accuracy and efficiency that off-the-shelf tools and generic LLMs simply cannot match. Powered by proprietary graph algorithms, transformer models and custom AI, the engine resolves more than 10 billion historic articles and over 5 million new articles a day, across more than 150 languages, into a single system of record for entity risk. 
By blending multiple data sources, including PEPs, sanctions, watchlists and adverse media, into one resolved profile, users gain a complete 3D view of risk. Risk lands on the right entity, with 98.7% accuracy, reducing the volume of alerts reaching an analyst by 99%. The engine continues to learn, so an analyst resolves an entity once and gets the benefit for the lifetime of that customer relationship. 
The latest innovations include enhancements to Screening Assistant, Ripjar’s agentic AI capability for alert triage, to further reduce routine alert handling, improve decision-making and increase risk coverage. Updates to ULTRA’s entity matching means customers can now better distinguish between parent organisations, subsidiaries and similarly named group entities. This removes guesswork and strengthens Screening Assistant’s ability to mimic human reasoning when deciding whether or not an alert relates to the exact entity. The update also extends Screening Assistant's handling of complex naming conventions, including Arabic names, to support more global use cases.
Ripjar has also enhanced ULTRA’s adverse media risk classifiers, which analyse each news article to determine if it relates to a specific risk and identify the person involved. The latest model upgrades ULTRA to a new generation of machine learning, improving the quality of existing classification and entity-resolution tasks.
ULTRA is proven in highly regulated and mission-critical environments where explainability and governance are vital. Every alert, decision and summary is backed by evidence, traceable to its source and held in an auditable system of record built for regulatory scrutiny.
Conrad Nicholas, Chief Product Officer at Ripjar, said: "ULTRA is one engine, but it runs multiple layers of AI, each performing a specific task: stripping out duplicate noise, resolving mentions across billions of articles into single entity profiles, and attributing risk to the right person. It works like a funnel, with each layer building on the last. What sets ULTRA apart is orchestrating these models at scale with explainability built in, so customers can trust the outcomes as well as benefit from more efficient screening.” 
Matt Mills, CEO at Ripjar, said: "Knowing who you’re doing business with is becoming more difficult. Sanctions change rapidly, adverse media multiplies and AI is enabling criminals to become more sophisticated. AI is vital but compliance teams need to understand and trust its decision making. We understand the importance of this in part due to our background in the UK’s intelligence services. ULTRA is the result of years of engineering and proven deployments and these latest innovations take explainability and performance to new levels.”

title: New Monzo Business Money Moves Report Reveals UK SMEs Are Gearing Up for Growth Despite Economic Headwinds
summary:
Monzo Business, the digital bank serving over one million business customers, today publishes its first Money Moves Report, taking a pulse check on the SMEs at the heart of the UK economy. Despite rising costs and economic uncertainty, businesses are feeling positive about the year ahead, with more than half (56%) of SMEs confident about their growth prospects over the next year.
Nearly two-thirds (62%) plan or hope to grow their teams over the coming year. But challenges remain: almost half (46%) naming rising costs as one of their biggest barriers to growth over the next year, followed by economic uncertainty (33%) and the tax burden (26%).
Monzo Business customer data also shows shifts in business spending, with bills up 12% over the past year while transport has remained flat.
The 53-minute a day admin burden  
It’s not just the economic environment that can get in the way of growth. Monzo’s research shows that the day-to-day complexity of running a business is creating another significant barrier to growth. UK SMEs currently spend an average of 53 minutes every working day on financial administration, including tasks such as processing invoices and expenses.
Nearly half of businesses (49%) say financial admin takes too long, with 39% saying it actively holds their business back from growing. For some, that means missing opportunities to invest in tech, equipment or premises (21%), pursuing new markets (20%), and hiring staff (18%).
Cutting admin could unlock the next wave of SME growth
Nearly two-thirds (63%) say simpler financial admin would free up time to focus on the things that matter most to their business, such as strategy, sales and building customer relationships. With extra time, one in three (33%) would pursue new customers or markets, 31% would invest in equipment, technology or premises and 26% would hire new staff.
Small businesses want more from their financial tools
Monzo Business customer data also shows spending on software has increased 15% over the last year. Yet, despite businesses putting more money towards technology, more than a third (37%) of SMEs say they are spending more time on financial admin than they were a year ago.
Just 24% agree that their bank actively helps them run their business rather than simply holding their money, as more than half (55%) say they often have to use other tools because their bank doesn’t offer everything they need to manage their finances. This points to growing demand for banking that makes running a business simpler. 
Jordan Shwide, General Manager at Monzo Business, said: “Small businesses are confident about the year ahead and thinking about how they can grow. However, running a business still comes with far too much financial admin, and our research shows that this isn’t simply an inconvenience - it can take time away from growth. 
“At Monzo Business, we want to be a partner in that growth, making business banking simpler and giving owners the tools to spend less time on admin and more time building their business.”
Monzo Business supports 1 in 6 UK businesses with tools designed to make managing finances simpler, from expense cards and tax pots to invoicing and payment links, which help businesses get paid 11 days faster. Read the full Monzo Business Money Moves Report at https://monzo.com/blog to explore the findings.

Banks Risk Losing $230 Billion in Payments Revenue as Stablecoins and Tokenized Deposits Go Mainstream
summary:
The global payments industry is approaching a tipping point. As stablecoins, tokenized deposits, and central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) move from experimentation to commercialization, banks face mounting pressure on traditional payments revenue pools. According to the Capgemini Research Institute’s World Payments Report 2027, these instruments are projected to account for approximately 4% of the global payments volume by 2030, impacting high-margin revenue streams such as foreign exchange spreads, correspondent banking, float income, and transaction processing fees.
Banks have prioritized payment innovation for corporate clients over the last three years with 60% identifying it as a strategic area of investment. However, only one in three corporate clients are satisfied with their primary banking partner, revealing a widening gap between what banks are delivering and what businesses increasingly expect.
Nearly three-quarters (74%) of corporates describe cross-border payments as slow, costly, and unpredictable. The end-to-the-end journey for corporate payments, from origination and transfer to confirmation and reconciliation, takes roughly 3.5 days. During that process, more than half (57%) report lacking access to live payment status, cash positions, or transparent pricing. Corporates rank predictability of settlement outcomes, real-time visibility into payment execution, and stronger protection against fraud among their most persistent unmet needs. As a result, corporates incur total costs equivalent to 2% of transaction value for a typical cross-border business-to-business (B2B) payment.
Now in its 22nd edition, the new report surveyed over 1,100 large corporates with revenues greater than USD 1 billion. On average, respondents indicate they operate in 14 markets, maintain 11 banking relationships, and conduct 34% of their B2B payment volume through cross-border transactions. Despite improvements in payment infrastructure, operational fragmentation remains the most defining challenge for corporate clients.
Accelerated intelligent money instruments emerge as a catalyst for transformation
Structural limitations in B2B payment infrastructure, regulatory clarity, and shifting market dynamics are driving the emergence of what the report defines as “accelerated intelligent money” – stablecoins, tokenized deposits, and CBDCs that enable money to do more than simply move between accounts. By supporting 24/7 execution, built-in rules and real-time settlement, these instruments can reduce friction during cross-border payment flows. The report estimates that widespread adoption could unlock as much as USD 4 trillion currently trapped in settlement and liquidity accounts – capital that generates little return and cannot be deployed for lending, investment or other productive uses.
Corporate demand is already building for this new generation of payment instruments and banks remain the preferred provider: 71% of corporates would choose a bank over a fintech for tokenized payments at equivalent cost and quality. However, that preference is not guaranteed. Nearly 60% of corporate clients are willing to source stablecoin services from non-bank providers if their banking partners fail to keep pace. This competitive erosion arrives as corporate clients report 36% of their B2B payment volume already flows through non-banks.
“The payments industry is entering its most significant period of disruption since the emergence of digital banking,” said Jeroen Hölscher, Global Head of Payment Services at Capgemini. “We are moving past the intelligent money hype cycle into a period where the economics and transaction volumes make it impossible for banks to remain on the sidelines. With $230 billion at stake, banks must decide what role they want to play in this emerging ecosystem. A select group of banks have already made their choice and are now shaping the standards and governance that will define the market. Those that act now will build lasting trust, capture new payment flows, and retain the corporate deposits that underpin their wider banking relationships.”
Banks identify tokenized deposits as key priority
As intelligent money moves toward commercialization, banks must define their strategic position in this ecosystem. The report finds that bank executives identify tokenized deposits as the top near-term priority for their ability to remain on balance sheets and fit within existing regulations. However, only 21% of banks – classified as leaders – are actively scaling at least one accelerated intelligent money instrument, while the remaining 79% of banks are still evaluating their position.
These high-achieving banks are focused on specific corporate use cases that address operational friction and monetize their value beyond transaction fees. The payoff is measurable as these leaders are three times more likely than mainstream banks to identify new revenue streams and expect to offset declining transaction revenue within 15 months, versus 25 months for rest of the industry. They are also more decisive: 33% of leaders aim to pursue a transformative market posture by shaping how the ecosystem operates, compared with 40% of mainstream banks that intend to take a reactive approach.
According to the report, since settlement with intelligent money is irrevocable, leaders place a premium on compliance by embedding it directly into execution before money moves. They outpace mainstream banks by 1.5 times on cross-network transaction monitoring and are 1.2 times more likely to both invest in AI-driven surveillance to flag unusual wallet behavior and implement real-time Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Know Your Customer (KYC) checks into transaction flows.
Yet even among leaders, foundational gaps remain. Just over half (56%) report having the talent and skills to build and maintain digital assets, technical readiness, and capabilities required to support tokenization, smart contracts, and interoperability across financial networks. Closing that gap will determine which banks are best positioned to move from experimentation to scale.

Midnite Partners with BR-DGE to Sharpen Payments Performance and Power International Expansion
summary:
BR-DGE, the payment optimisation platform built for the demands of gaming and sports betting, has partnered with Midnite, the hyper-growth UK sportsbook and casino operator. 
Midnite is known for a fast, friction-free app experience and BR-DGE will bring that same standard to its payments stack, strengthening resilience, optimising performance for pay-ins and payouts, and underpinning a smooth customer experience. 
Pairing Midnite’s product-led, mobile-first platform with BR-DGE’s sector expertise gives their payments team a partner that understands the operational and regulatory realities of gaming at every stage of a transaction.
Before working with BR-DGE, Midnite operated via direct integrations with payment providers in the UK and Ireland. That setup served the business well while it was establishing itself, but rapid growth and ambitious expansion plans meant payments needed to keep pace with the speed and simplicity Midnite already delivers everywhere else in its app. 
As a trailblazer in the industry, Midnite took the same innovative approach to its payment strategy as it has to every other aspect of its business, matching its scaling journey and its customers’ expectations.
Moving to BR-DGE addressed that directly. Midnite was able to bring TrueLayer’s Pay By Bank payments almost immediately through BR-DGE’s existing connectivity, with further alternative payment methods already in the implementation phase through the platform. As Midnite continues to execute ambitious growth plans, BR-DGE will also enable new payment options, to give Midnite the payment setup it needs to serve new markets from day one.
Midnite’s rapid growth also demands further PSP connectivity, which the operator will add through BR-DGE in due course. This will also allow Midnite to benefit from BR-DGE’s smart routing capabilities, supporting optimisation across costs, acceptance rates and uptime, for deposits and withdrawals. 
Centralised tokenisation via BR-DGE Vault will keep stored card details portable across both processors, so the change doesn’t mean re-tokenising players or disrupting the checkout experience they’re used to.
Alongside routing, tokenisation and connectivity, Midnite will benefit from BR-DGE’s gaming-specific performance benchmarking and market insights. This intelligence, drawn from BR-DGE’s gaming merchant base (spanning multiple regulated markets, including the UK, Ireland, North America, Europe and Australia) and modelling capabilities, gives Midnite actionable insight on how payment journeys can be improved, to balance cost, security, acceptance and the customer experience.
Jacob Spencer, Chief Revenue Officer at BR-DGE, said: “Midnite built a strong platform on a single PSP, which worked well domestically but limited how quickly they could add new payment methods or move into new markets. Moving to an independent orchestration layer mitigates that technical debt in one step, giving Midnite the scalability they need to match their success and ambitions.
“BR-DGE’s track record and data intelligence capabilities will augment and enrich our orchestration capabilities, enabling Midnite to direct every transaction to achieve optimal performance, even as their business evolves and grows.”
Christian Huynh, Lead Product Manager, Midnite said: “At Midnite, we want every part of the experience to feel built different, and payments are no exception. We’re focused on creating payment experiences that delight our customers, while building the flexibility to innovate quickly and bring the same great experience to new markets as we grow.”
The partnership adds Midnite to a growing roster of gaming operators that rely on BR-DGE’s independent orchestration layer and data intelligence, reinforcing BR-DGE’s position as the leading payment optimisation platform for the gaming sector.

Teya Partners with ClearBank to Launch High-Yield Savings Account for Local Businesses
summary:
Teya, the financial services provider supporting local businesses across Europe, today launches Savings Pots, a new savings account with interest paid daily built into the Teya Business Account and powered by ClearBank, the enabler of real-time clearing and embedded banking. 
Now available to existing Teya Business Account holders in the UK, Savings Pots allows business-owners to open pots earning 3% AER (variable) with interest calculated and paid daily. Money in a pot remains instantly accessible, so business-owners can move funds in or out at any time without losing flexibility or facing withdrawal delays.
Teya’s Savings Pots feature has been designed specifically to meet the day-to-day needs of local businesses. It gives them the freedom to set money aside, whether for tax bills, growth plans or a rainy day, all while earning interest, directly within the app they already use.
Sahithya Vemana, Head of Banking at Teya, said: “Local businesses should be able to earn a competitive return, keep their money accessible and manage their finances simply in one place. More than 50% of members we interviewed told us they don’t earn interest on their free cash because they can’t be bothered with the hassle of managing money across multiple accounts. With Savings Pots, the money a business earns through Teya moves seamlessly from payments into savings, earns interest that is accrued and paid every day and remains instantly accessible when needed, all within Teya, with no separate savings relationship to manage or reconcile.”
Emma Hagan, CEO of ClearBank UK, said: “Teya is an ambitious and innovative business that is moving quickly to give local businesses better ways to manage their money. This launch shows what is possible when two fast-moving businesses work together: combining Teya’s understanding of its customers with ClearBank’s flexible, scalable and resilient banking infrastructure to bring useful new products to market at pace. We’re excited to support Teya as it continues to develop its offering and help local businesses make more of their money.”
Teya is delivering Savings Pots through ClearBank’s Embedded Banking proposition, enabling FSCS-protected, interest-bearing savings powered by ClearBank as a third-party UK authorised bank.
Carl Hirschson, Senior Product Manager at Teya, said: "Integration speed comes down to the quality of what you're building on. We looked at several ways of doing this and went with ClearBank because their banking infrastructure layer is something we can rely on and build on top of. That's why Savings Pots and our upcoming premium savings product were both built in four months rather than a year. Two products built on one integration."
The launch of Savings Pots is the first savings product from the partnership, with more to follow. It comes after other major product upgrades from Teya, including a new Business Account that allows business-owners to automate spend management, earn cashback on all their team members’ day-to-day spending and manage everything through one app, and the new Teya Pro, a next-generation card machine that completes transactions in under 1.7 seconds.
Earlier this month, Teya was selected by the Financial Conduct Authority for the solo-regulated track of its flagship Scale-up Unit, joining ClearBank, which was selected for the Unit’s first cohort of dual-regulated firms in February 2026.
